academic_translation: That is because it is neither a phenomenon nor the absence of a phenomenon.
translation: "That is because it is not a thing, and it is also not the absence of a thing."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because noble persons are distinguished by the unconditioned.
translation: "Why is that? Because noble persons are known by what is not made by causes."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?

locked_terms.use: son of a good family or daughter of a good family

translation: If a son of a good family or daughter of a good family filled this world realm, a universe of a billion worlds, with the seven precious things and gave it as a gift, do you think that son of a good family or daughter of a good family would make a great pile of stored-up goodness from doing that?

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, Blessed One, it would be much.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, it would be a lot."

academic_translation: Sugata, it would be much.
translation: "Well-Gone One, it would be a lot."

academic_translation: That son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis.

locked_terms.use: son of a good family or daughter of a good family

translation: "That son of a good family or daughter of a good family would make a great pile of stored-up goodness from that."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because that very mass of merit is not a mass.
translation: "Why is that? It is because that very pile of stored-up goodness is not a pile."

academic_translation: Therefore, the Tathāgata spoke of "a mass of merit, a mass of merit."
translation: "That is why the Thus-Gone One spoke of a pile of stored-up goodness, a pile of stored-up goodness."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, compared to a son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, if someone takes up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse, explains it to others, and perfectly demonstrates it, they will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.

locked_terms.use: son of a good family or daughter of a good family

translation: The Blessed One said: "Subhuti, imagine a son of a good family or daughter of a good family. They fill this world realm, a universe of a billion worlds, with the seven precious things. Then they give it as a gift. Now imagine someone else. They learn just a four-line verse from this lesson on the teaching. They explain it to others and show it perfectly. That person will create a much larger pile of stored-up goodness. It will be too huge to count or measure."

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, the unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening of the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas, arises from this,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, the highest, complete awakening of the Thus-Gone Ones, the worthy ones, and the complete Buddhas comes from this,

academic_translation: because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.
translation: because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what are called "qualities of a Buddha, qualities of a Buddha," it is because the Tathāgata spoke of those qualities of a Buddha as non-existent;
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, as for what are called 'qualities of a Buddha, qualities of a Buddha,' the Thus-Gone One said those qualities of a Buddha do not exist.

academic_translation: therefore they are called "qualities of a Buddha."
translation: That is why they are called 'qualities of a Buddha.'"

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Does a stream-enterer think: I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer?
translation: Does a stream-enterer think, "I have gotten the fruit of a stream-enterer"?

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, it is not so."

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because he has not entered into anything.
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because he has not entered into anything.

academic_translation: Therefore, he is called a stream-enterer.
translation: That is why he is called a stream-enterer.

tibetan: གཟུགས་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཞུགས། སྒྲ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། དྲི་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། རོ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། རེག་བྱ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཞུགས་ཏེ།
academic_translation: He has not entered into forms, nor into sounds, nor into smells, nor into tastes, nor into tangible objects, nor has he entered into phenomena.
translation: He has not entered into shapes, or sounds, or smells, or tastes, or things that are touched. He has not entered into things.

academic_translation: Therefore, he is called a "stream-enterer."
translation: That is why they are called a stream-enterer.

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think that he had attained the fruit of a stream-enterer, that itself would be his grasping at a self.
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer thought they gained the fruit of a stream-enterer, that would be clinging to a self.

academic_translation: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
translation: It would be clinging to a living being, clinging to a life, and clinging to a person.

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: Does a once-returner think that he has attained the fruit of a once-returner?
translation: Does a once-returner think they have gained the fruit of a once-returner?

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of a once-returner.
translation: Why is that? Because there is no thing that has entered the state of a once-returner.

academic_translation: Therefore, he is called a once-returner.
translation: That is why he is called a once-returner.

academic_translation: Blessed One, if a once-returner were to think, 'I have attained the fruit of a once-returner,' that itself would be his grasping at a self.
translation: Blessed One, if a once-returner thought, 'I have gained the fruit of a once-returner,' that would be clinging to a self.

academic_translation: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
translation: It would be clinging to a living being, clinging to a life, and clinging to a person.

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Does a non-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a non-returner'?"
translation: Does a non-returner think, 'I have gained the fruit of a non-returner'?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, Blessed One, that is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of a non-returner.
translation: "Why is that? Because there is no thing at all that has entered the state of a non-returner."

academic_translation: Therefore, he is called a non-returner.
translation: "That is why he is called a non-returner."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, what do you think?"

academic_translation: Does an arhat think, I have attained arhatship?
translation: "Does a worthy one think, 'I have reached the state of a worthy one'?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, Blessed One, that is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, that is not so."

academic_translation: Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that is called an arhat.
translation: Why is that? It is because there is no thing at all that is called a worthy one.

academic_translation: Blessed One, if an arhat were to think, 'I have obtained arhatship,' that itself would be his grasping at a self,
translation: Blessed One, if a worthy one thought, 'I have gained the state of a worthy one,' that would be clinging to a self.
